\[
E = \lvert \nabla (G_\sigma * Y) \rvert,
\qquad
L(x) = \text{marker whose flood reaches } x \text{ first}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(E\): The elevation, the gradient magnitude
- \(L(x)\): The region of pixel x

The elevation E is the gradient magnitude of the blurred luma Y, so edges are ridges. The markers replace the minima of the plain watershed. Each 8-connected part of the selection is one marker, and with the border marker, the edge of the image outside the selection is another. Water rises from the markers only, so no region starts anywhere else. Each pixel joins the flood that reaches it first, and floods meet on the ridges between the markers. Meyer and Beucher made markers the way to tell the watershed which objects to find.
